thread.title: Lumentum Pops As Apple Seen Pushing Augmented Reality Into New iPhones

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Lumentum Pops As Apple Seen Pushing Augmented Reality Into New iPhones
text:
Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) stock jumped on Friday, hitting a buy point, as one Apple ( AAPL ) follower speculated that upcoming iPhones will feature more 3D sensors for augmented reality apps.
X Lumentum is a supplier of 3D sensors to Apple, which uses the components in the current iPhone X to support facial recognition for unlocking screens. Apple's iPhone X doesn't have 3D sensors to support AR apps.
Apple in December awarded Lumentum rival Finisar ( FNSR ) a $390 million contract for future orders.
Finisar management commentary on its earnings call late Thursday may have signaled that Apple's new iPhones coming out later this year will have more 3D sensors, Gene Munster, a managing partner at Loup Ventures, said in a blog.
"We believe (Finisar) management's comments around a second-half 2018 ramp remains positive for Apple's new iPhone launch this fall, where we expect the company to introduce multiple new iPhones and all will incorporate 3D sensing technology," Munster said. "This in turn confirms that Apple will make augmented reality (AR) a core feature in all new iPhones this fall."
Other analysts say 3D sensors also will be built in upcoming iPad tablets.
Lumentum currently is supplying the lion's share of 3D sensor devices, called vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSEL), to Apple, analysts say.
Lumentum stock rose 5.5% to 68.98 on the stock market today , clearing a technical buy point of 68.73. Volume was above average, but not huge.
Weak demand for optical devices built into telecom networks has been a drag on Lumentum stock, which has rebounded from lows set in early February.

Finisar reported fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that missed views, with April-quarter guidance also below expectations.
Finisar shares sank 4.5% t0 19.30 on Friday. Finisar has been set back by pricing pressure in the data center market as well as a slowdown in China orders, analysts say.
